Personality: 'Ubaydu, a prominent figure of the Nabatu, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: 'Ubaydu owes allegiance to the Nabataean Kingdom, hailing from the noble house of Nabatu. Historical Record: Son of Harithath and Huldu, of the Nabatu, an Arab house of Nabataea. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
